disease_label_per_paper: Acute right epididymo-orchitis complicated by pampiniform plexus thrombosis
presentation_summary: 41-year-old married man with no known chronic medical illness or prior surgical procedures presented to the emergency department with right testicular pain and dysuria that began two days earlier.
Pain was initially mild, gradually increased in severity, and was associated with right hemiscrotal swelling.
He had a remote prior episode of epididymo-orchitis treated with oral antibiotics years earlier.
He denied fever, urethral discharge, recent illegal sexual contact, and upper respiratory tract disease; apart from dysuria he denied other lower urinary tract manifestations.

Examination showed normal external genitalia and meatus, enlarged tender right scrotum, palpable testes bilaterally, and thick tender right epididymis; cremasteric reflex and Prehn testing favored epididymitis.

Bedside urine dipstick was nitrite-positive, basic blood work was unremarkable, and emergency scrotal ultrasound showed increased right testicular vascularity with epididymal enlargement and no varicocele.

actual_treatment: pre-presentation oral antibiotics from primary care
piperacillin-tazobactam based on culture sensitivity profile
conservative management for pampiniform plexus thrombosis without therapeutic anticoagulation

outcome.source_text_value: condition improved dramatically, discharged home, and six-week follow-up ultrasound showed complete thrombus resolution

quality_warnings: E. coli culture identity, susceptibility profile, post-treatment negative culture, pampiniform thrombosis, and follow-up response are preserved as non-ranking evidence.
No fever and absent urethral discharge are kept as presentation evidence; they do not exclude epididymo-orchitis.
The rare pampiniform plexus thrombosis complication is not used to make the initial presentation diagnosis.
